target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners and, later, patients with obesity, metabolic and inflammatory disease via its own antibody drugs
problem: Many drug targets are GPCRs that need to be switched on, not just blocked, and standard antibody screens select for binding rather than activity.
business_model: Preclinical biotech: own pipeline plus platform collaborations with pharma

founders.name: Richard Yu
education: PhD 2000 Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry, Yale
BA 1993 Biophysics and Computer Science, UC Berkeley
previous_startups: GPB (algae biofuel, co-founded 2008, outcome not stated)

founders.name: Gustavo Pesce
founders.background_notes: Company site says Yu met him at the Molecular Sciences Institute and that they co-founded the company.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering yeast to link cell survival to antibody activity and screening about 100 million antibodies per experiment is research grade biology.

defensibility.rationale: A functional selection platform plus patents and partner data are hard to copy, though drug discovery outcomes depend on clinical results.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying found; Pfizer signed a research collaboration with Abalone in January 2026 per a press release.

market_need_then: Antibodies that activate GPCRs were an unmet need for difficult targets, and obesity drugs became a large market. NIH SBIR grants in 2021 and 2022 funded programs for inflammatory bowel disease and endometriosis pain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'Antibody agonists for the targets that matter most'

brand_strength.rationale: Science led B2B brand; no press or community evidence about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Abalone Bio is a preclinical biotech that has won grants and pharma partners. It signed a research collaboration with Pfizer in January 2026, with Sihuan Pharmaceutical on an obesity drug in October 2025 and with the University of Pennsylvania in March 2025 per press listings. Equity funding is unclear, so how well it raised is unknown. No shutdown or acquisition found.
notes: Funding is unverified: Pharmaletter says $125K from YC in 2020 and an $800K America's Seed Fund grant in 2019; Seedtable $150K seed in March 2020; a yespress page claims a $3M seed led by Horizons Ventures; Caplight shows a headline for a $16M Series A dated April 2024 with an empty table and total funding of $11.07M; YC page cites $7M non-dilutive grants. None confirmed by a filing or press release, so no rounds recorded. Founding year 2017 or 2018 across sources. Competitor search found no sources dated near 2020 so the list is empty. The company site footer mentions Codon65 but this is not explained. Completeness pass: each round rests on a single database or outlet (Pharmaletter, CB Insights, Caplight). Pharmaletter gives YC 125K for the 2020 seed while CB Insights gives 150K on Mar 17 2020. Company states 7M in non-dilutive grants, more than the grants recorded; Caplight total 11.07M and CB Insights 1.12M conflict, so the gap is unresolved.
